summary: Executed full media-storage verification (backend + frontend) against public preview URL: real image uploads (JPG/PNG/WebP/GIF), rejection matrix, Mongo persistence checks, object-storage fresh-session read, admin CMS upload flows, public render verification, responsive checks, and regression commands (pytest/typecheck/build). critical.issue: At the public endpoint, Cache-Control is `no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate` instead of expected long-lived cache (`public, max-age=31536000, immutable`). Backend code sets immutable cache, but response observed externally is rewritten. This caused 4/4 format tests to fail on cache-header assertion.

rca of the issue: RCA: Cache-policy failure is likely outside application route logic. read_image() sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, but external responses consistently show `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate` while other custom headers (nosniff/CSP) survive. This pattern indicates ingress/edge/proxy middleware rewriting Cache-Control for API routes. Mitigation: update edge rule for /api/media/* to preserve app Cache-Control (or set explicit override to immutable). Reproduction: upload any valid image -> GET returned /api/media/{id} -> inspect headers at preview domain.
